bodyweight_squat.name: Bodyweight Squat
bodyweight_squat.cue: Feet about shoulder width, sit down between the hips. Hip crease below the knee, chest tall, drive through the whole foot.

back_squat.name: Back Squat
back_squat.cue: Bar on the back, brace, sit between the hips. Hip crease below the knee, knees tracking over the toes.

reverse_nordic.name: Assisted Reverse Nordic Curl
reverse_nordic.cue: Knees-over-toes eccentric; assist with band or hands.

coaching.why: One leg at a time — the fastest way to find and fix a weak side. It waits until the knee says yes.
cues: Back foot on the bench, front foot a long stride out.
Drop straight down, front thigh towards parallel.
All the weight through the front heel.
mistakes: Starting this before the knee is ready. It is parked until week nine at the earliest.

coaching.why: The counterweight at your chest is what makes a squat knee-friendly for a beginner.
cues: Hold the bell at chest height, elbows tucked in.
Sit down between the hips, chest tall, to the bench.
Drive up through the whole foot.
mistakes: Letting the elbows drift out and the chest fold. The bell stays glued to your sternum.

sissy_squat.name: Sissy Squat
sissy_squat.cue: Knees forward, lean back — quad-focused. (future anchor)

deadlift.name: Deadlift
deadlift.cue: Brace, push floor away, neutral spine.

single_leg_rdl.name: Single-Leg RDL
single_leg_rdl.cue: Hinge on one leg, square hips, hamstring stretch.

coaching.why: Hamstrings, balance, and a hip that finally works one side at a time.
cues: Soft knee on the standing leg. It stays soft, it does not bend more.
Hinge until you feel the hamstring, back leg rising behind you.
Hips stay square to the floor. Do not let the back hip roll open.
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower. Stop where the hamstring stops you.

coaching.why: The glute bridge with the bit that actually makes the outer glute work.
cues: Band above the knees. Press out into it the whole time.
Squeeze hard at the top for one second.

banded_sidewalk.name: Banded Lateral Walks
banded_sidewalk.cue: Band at knees, stay low, continuous side-steps.

hip_thrust.name: Hip Thrust
hip_thrust.cue: Chin tucked, full lockout, glute squeeze.

nordic_curl.name: Nordic Curl
nordic_curl.cue: Control the eccentric; progress ROM → load.

tibialis_raise.name: Tibialis Raise
tibialis_raise.cue: Toes up against wall, full ROM.

bench_press.name: Bench Press
bench_press.cue: Shoulder blades pinned to the bench, feet down. Bar to the sternum, elbows about 45 degrees, press to lockout.

overhead_press.name: Overhead Press
overhead_press.cue: Standing and strict. Ribs down, squeeze the glutes, press until the arms are by the ears. No leg drive.

wall_push_up.name: Wall Push-Up
wall_push_up.cue: Hands on wall at chest height, feet a step back. Body straight. Press into wall, control the return. The further your feet, the harder.

incline_push_up.name: Incline Push-Up
incline_push_up.cue: Hands on elevated surface. Great entry-level push pattern. Elbows 45°. Chest to bench.

knee_push_up.name: Knee Push-Up
knee_push_up.cue: From knees, hands shoulder-width, body straight from knees to head. Chest to floor. Lock arms at top. No hip pike — this is a real push-up scaled.

pike_hold.name: Pike Hold
pike_hold.cue: Inverted V position, straight arms, push floor away. Hold position. Builds wrist endurance and shoulder overhead strength.

shorties.name: Shorties
shorties.cue: Bottom-half partial push-ups — chest near floor to mid-range, no lockout at top. Continuous tension, deep stretch on the chest, no rest. Alternative: top-half pulses (upper 50%, no chest touch) — different stimulus, less stretch. Both = killer pump tools after full push-ups.

bench_dip.name: Bench Dip
bench_dip.cue: Hands behind on bench, feet on floor or elevated. Full depth. Great entry-level dip.

dip_support_hold.name: Dip Support Hold
dip_support_hold.cue: Top of the dip position — arms locked, shoulders depressed and packed, body upright. Hold full bodyweight without bending arms. The entry test for dip work. Build 30-60s before attempting reps.

frog_stand.name: Frog Stand
frog_stand.cue: Hands shoulder-width, knees resting on elbows/triceps. Lean forward and lift feet. First real planche shape — accessible to beginners. Build to 30s.

pike_pulses.name: Pike Pulses
pike_pulses.cue: Sit in pike (legs straight together). Actively pulse torso DOWN toward legs using hip flexors only — not gravity bounce. 20-30 reps. Key compression warm-up before handstand or L-sit work.

pushup.name: Push-ups
pushup.cue: Elbows 45°, chest to floor, protract fully at top. Active core throughout.

coaching.why: The whole upper body in one movement. Everything scales from here.
cues: Hands on the bench to start — the higher the hands, the easier it is.
One line from ear to heel. Squeeze the glutes.
Elbows back at about 45°, not flared out to the sides.
mistakes: Hips sagging first. If they do, raise the hands. Do not cut the reps.

seated_knee_tuck_raises.name: Seated Knee Tuck Raises
seated_knee_tuck_raises.cue: Sit on floor or parallettes, hands beside hips, arms straight. Pull knees to chest explosively, hold 1-2s at top. Lower with control. Builds the strength needed for L-sit and press to handstand.

banded_dip.name: Banded Dip
banded_dip.cue: Loop a resistance band over the parallel bars, knees rest in the band loop. The band assists the press out of the bottom. Choose band tension so you can do 5-8 reps unbroken. Progress by switching to a lighter band.

db_preacher_curl.name: DB Preacher Curl
db_preacher_curl.cue: Use a preacher bench (or any padded incline). Isolate the bicep — curl with maximum tension and a controlled lower. Focus on the BOTTOM lockout — that is where the bicep tendon takes load. Specifically conditions the bicep tendon against hyperextension injuries that planche straight-arm pressure causes. Bulletproofs the elbow for planche work.

decline_push_up.name: Decline Push-Up
decline_push_up.cue: Feet elevated, lead with chest. Straight body from head to heels.

dip_bottom_hold.name: Dip Bottom Hold
dip_bottom_hold.cue: Bottom of the dip — shoulder below elbow, controlled tension. Hold here to build strength at the hardest position. Start at 5-10s holds, build to 30s.

dip_negative.name: Dip Negative
dip_negative.cue: Start at the top of the dip (arms locked). Lower yourself slowly — 4-5 seconds down to the bottom. Step off and reset. Eccentric work builds the strength to press up. 3-5 negatives per set.

feet_on_wall_90_degree.name: Feet on Wall 90 Degree
feet_on_wall_90_degree.cue: Hands on floor ~1 foot from wall, feet walked up the wall to hip height — body forms a 90° angle. Hold position with shoulders stacked. The L-shape primes the overhead press pattern for HSPU work.

full_burpee.name: Full Burpee
full_burpee.cue: Squat → hands → jump back → chest to floor (full push-up) → jump feet in → squat → explosive jump with arms overhead. One fluid motion. Land soft every rep. No shortcuts — full range is the entire point.

hindu_push_up.name: Hindu Push-Up
hindu_push_up.cue: Start in pike. Arc chest close to ground forward into upward dog, push to lockout. Reverse the arc back to pike. Not a push-up — it's a full shoulder arc wave. Control the spine extension at the top.

pike_lean.name: Pike Lean
pike_lean.cue: From pike, shift shoulders FORWARD over wrists. No balance assist — pure strength. The further you lean, the harder it gets.

pike_push_up.name: Pike Push-Up
pike_push_up.cue: Hips high, head goes through arms at bottom, press overhead.

ring_support_hold.name: Ring Support Hold
ring_support_hold.cue: Straight arms, rings turned out at bottom (RTO). Shoulders depressed and packed. Build to 30-60s before ring dips.

straight_bar_push_up.name: Straight Bar Push-Up
straight_bar_push_up.cue: Hands on parallettes or a fixed barbell. Greater depth than floor — chest drops well below hand level. Full scapular protraction at top. Narrow grip, elbows at 45°. Excellent shoulder health and chest stimulus.

bottoms_up_kb_hold.name: Bottoms-Up KB Hold
bottoms_up_kb_hold.cue: Kettlebell upside-down at shoulder, bell pointing to ceiling. Wrist neutral, elbow tucked. The bell wants to flop — your grip + shoulder stabilizers fight for the line. 20–40 sec each hand. Brutal for shoulder stability + grip.

chest_to_wall_handstand_hold.name: Chest-to-Wall Handstand Hold
chest_to_wall_handstand_hold.cue: Face the wall. Walk up into handstand with the chest, thighs and feet near the wall (NOT the back). Locked elbows, elevated scapula. Only the feet touch the wall — body straight line. Trains the same alignment as freestanding handstand without the balance demand.

deadstop_pushup.name: Dead-Stop Push-up
deadstop_pushup.cue: Lower all the way to the floor. Lift hands off — full tension release. Reset. Press from zero. No stretch reflex, no momentum. Every rep is a fresh max effort. Brutally effective for pure chest strength.

deep_pike_pushup.name: Deep Parallette Pike Push-Up
deep_pike_pushup.cue: Hips stacked, deep ROM off parallettes.

diamond_push_up.name: Diamond Push-Up
diamond_push_up.cue: Hands form diamond, elbows track back, squeeze triceps hard at lockout.

dip.name: Dip
dip.cue: Slight lean for chest, upright for triceps. Full depth. No shoulder shrug.

elephant_walk.name: Elephant Walk
elephant_walk.cue: Start in pike/downward dog. Walk hands backward toward feet, keeping legs as straight as possible and hips high. Alternate hand steps. Bridges pike strength to press to handstand.

elevated_pike_lean.name: Elevated Pike Lean
elevated_pike_lean.cue: Feet elevated on bench. Pike lean forward — more load through the arms due to elevation.

elevated_pike_push_up.name: Elevated Pike Push-Up
elevated_pike_push_up.cue: Feet elevated on bench in pike position. Press overhead. Closer to handstand angle than floor pike push-up.

handstand_kick_ups.name: Handstand Kick-Ups
handstand_kick_ups.cue: Practice the dynamic entry to freestanding handstand. Kick up, find balance briefly, come down. Reps = entries. Use wall nearby for safety.

navy_seal_push_up_3_pump.name: Navy Seal Push-Up (3 pump)
navy_seal_push_up_3_pump.cue: At the bottom of each push-up, do 3 small partial pumps (chest stays an inch off floor) before pressing back to lockout. 1 set = 3 pumps + 1 full rep. Time-under-tension at the hardest position. Brutal for chest endurance.

planche_lean.name: Planche Lean
planche_lean.cue: Arms locked, lean forward until shoulders over or past wrists. Go further each week.

ring_push_up.name: Ring Push-Up
ring_push_up.cue: Keep rings close, turn out (RTO) at lockout. Serratus fires hard.

seated_straight_leg_raises.name: Seated Straight Leg Raises
seated_straight_leg_raises.cue: Sit on floor or parallettes, arms straight beside hips, scapula depressed. Raise straight legs up as high as possible. Lower with control. Pure compression strength and active hamstring flexibility.

straddle_leg_lifts.name: Straddle Leg Lifts
straddle_leg_lifts.cue: Sit, legs straddled wide. Lift both legs in straddle — keeping knees straight. Develops active compression + straddle flexibility simultaneously. Key for press to handstand.

straight_arm_db_fly.name: Straight-Arm DB Fly
straight_arm_db_fly.cue: Standing or slightly leaning forward, hold light DBs at sides with arms locked straight. Raise dumbbells HORIZONTALLY out to the sides while maintaining strict scapular protraction (push the floor away). Keep the path of movement near your waistline — simulates planche load through the same shoulder angle. ALTERNATIVE: use a band anchored at hip height — pull straight out to the side with same form.

t_rotation_push_up.name: T-Rotation Push-Up
t_rotation_push_up.cue: Push-up, then rotate body into a side plank and raise top arm straight up forming a T. Alternate sides. Push + anti-rotation in one movement.

wall_walk.name: Wall Walk
wall_walk.cue: Start in push-up position. Walk feet up wall and hands in toward wall simultaneously until chest is close to wall. Walk back down with control.

ring_pushup.name: Weighted Deep Ring Push-Up
ring_pushup.cue: Deep ROM, turn rings out at top. (Phase-2 push anchor)

zanetti_db_press.name: Zanetti DB Press
zanetti_db_press.cue: Lie back on a bench. Hold dumbbells with arms STRAIGHT (elbows locked) at hip level. Raise the weights up to a 45° angle above the hips, then lower slowly. Replicates the exact straight-arm shoulder flexion required for planche. ALTERNATIVE: anchor a resistance band low and pull with straight arms to the same 45° endpoint — same pattern, scalable load.

archer_complex.name: Archer Complex
archer_complex.cue: Alternating: unilateral ring row right → push-up → ring row left = 1 rep. Scapular control on each row. Hips square. The push-up is the controlled reset between rows. Pull elbow back — not out.

back_to_wall_handstand_hold.name: Back-to-Wall Handstand Hold
back_to_wall_handstand_hold.cue: Kick up facing AWAY from wall. Heels lightly touch wall. Good entry to handstand balance work.

burpee_pull_up.name: Burpee Pull-Up
burpee_pull_up.cue: Full burpee directly below the bar. Use the jump momentum to flow into the pull-up — don't pause between. Pull to chin over bar. Land softly on descent. One continuous fluid motion.

diamond_push_up_on_kettlebell.name: Diamond Push-Up on Kettlebell
diamond_push_up_on_kettlebell.cue: Diamond grip on a single KB handle. Lower deep — the KB elevates your hands giving extra ROM. Elbows track tight. Squeeze hard at top. Bell stability adds a hidden challenge.

frog_planche.name: Frog Planche
frog_planche.cue: Between Tuck and Advanced Tuck. Knees rest lightly on the outside of your elbows while leaning forward. Slowly pull knees away from the arms as you gain strength. The bridge that lets you load planche torque without full bodyweight commitment.

navy_seal_burpee.name: Navy Seal Burpee
navy_seal_burpee.cue: 3 push-ups at bottom of each burpee, then jump + clap. Punishing and effective.

pike_lean_on_parallettes.name: Pike Lean on Parallettes
pike_lean_on_parallettes.cue: Parallettes allow DEEPER lean = greater forward lean angle = more horizontal load. Far harder than floor version. Directly bridges to planche and handstand strength.

turkish_get_up.name: Turkish Get-Up
turkish_get_up.cue: Eyes on the bell every second of the movement. 7 steps up, 7 down. Never rush a step. Drive through heel not knee on the lunge. Wrist locked and packed throughout the entire movement.

wall_handstand.name: Wall Handstand
wall_handstand.cue: Straight line ears-hips-heels. Active shoulders (push floor away). Gaze at floor.

archer_push_up.name: Archer Push-Up
archer_push_up.cue: Shift weight to one arm, other arm straight for balance. Hips square.

devil_s_press.name: Devil's Press
devil_s_press.cue: Burpee down, chest touches floor. Explosive hip hinge to snatch both DBs overhead in one motion. Arms stay straight on the swing up. Control the descent — don't drop.

half_one_arm_push_up.name: Half One-Arm Push-Up
half_one_arm_push_up.cue: Working arm shoulder-width, free hand on a low box (so the body angle is steeper than incline but easier than full one-arm). Slow descent on one arm only. The box absorbs less weight as it lowers.

open_tuck_planche.name: Open Tuck Planche
open_tuck_planche.cue: Knees off the chest, knees still bent. Lower back should flatten completely — hips no longer protected by the tuck. The jump from this to Adv Tuck is where most people stall; do not skip it.

planche_lean_raises.name: Planche Lean Raises
planche_lean_raises.cue: Start in a standard planche lean. Press hard through your shoulders WHILE walking or sliding your feet forward — forcing your hips to elevate until your toes lightly float off the floor. The dynamic version of planche lean that introduces the hip lift.

ring_dip.name: Ring Dip
ring_dip.cue: Full lockout with RTO. Rings tight to body. Control the descent.

ring_dip_knee_raise.name: Ring Dip + Knee Raise
ring_dip_knee_raise.cue: Full ring dip → hold at top → compress knees to chest. Shoulders packed. RTO at lockout. The knee raise is active compression — not a swing. Link the push and core as one unit.

tuck_planche_hold.name: Tuck Planche Hold
tuck_planche_hold.cue: Wrists turned out, shoulders over wrists, max protraction, knees tight to chest.

adv_tuck_planche.name: Adv. Tuck Planche
adv_tuck_planche.cue: Back flat, legs tuck below hips. 5s max holds with full rest.

assisted_one_arm_push_up.name: Assisted One-Arm Push-Up
assisted_one_arm_push_up.cue: Use a band looped overhead, hooked under the chest to unload some bodyweight, OR free hand resting LIGHTLY on a low surface for balance only (not bearing weight). Working arm does the work.

bulgarian_dip.name: Bulgarian Dip
bulgarian_dip.cue: On rings. From the top of a ring dip, rotate the rings outward and turn the palms forward at the top (Bulgarian press). Adds rotational shoulder stability + tricep load. Slow tempo only.

chest_to_wall_deficit_hspu.name: Chest-to-Wall Deficit HSPU
chest_to_wall_deficit_hspu.cue: Hands on parallettes facing the wall, chest-to-wall handstand position. Lower your head BELOW the level of your hands (the deficit). Press back up to lockout. Builds the deepest range of motion needed for full HSPU.

l_sit_push_back_to_planche.name: L-Sit Push-Back to Planche
l_sit_push_back_to_planche.cue: Start in L-sit or tuck sit on parallettes. Fluidly push hips backward and upward through a tuck planche, aiming to extend into straddle or full planche for a brief 1-2 second hold. Trains the dynamic entry to planche.

man_maker.name: Man-Maker
man_maker.cue: Push-up → row right → row left → feet jump in → clean → squat → overhead press. One rep = all 7 steps. Hips square during rows. Drive from legs into the press.

one_arm_push_up.name: One-Arm Push-Up
one_arm_push_up.cue: Feet wide, hips square. 3s descent. Master archer push-up first.

pseudo_planche_push_up.name: Pseudo Planche Push-Up
pseudo_planche_push_up.cue: Hands turned out, lean forward — shoulders over wrists. Maintain hollow body.

russian_dip.name: Russian Dip
russian_dip.cue: Parallel bar dip. At the bottom, lower onto your forearms (forearms touch the bars). Press back up to the dip start — drive through forearms then hands. Brutal triceps + shoulder control. Start with 1-3 reps, build slowly.

semi_straddle_planche.name: Semi-Straddle Planche
semi_straddle_planche.cue: Also called Closed Straddle. Legs spread wide BUT knees bent at 90°. Reduces lever length while training hip abduction. The final bridge before Full Straddle.

single_leg_planche.name: Single-Leg Planche
single_leg_planche.cue: From an Adv Tuck, extend exactly ONE leg straight back; keep the other tightly tucked. Alternate legs per set. This bridges the gap from Adv Tuck directly to Straddle Planche by training one half of the lever at a time.

straight_arm_dip_rings.name: Straight-Arm Dip (Rings)
straight_arm_dip_rings.cue: From RTO ring support hold, lean shoulders forward over (or past) the rings. Arms stay LOCKED straight throughout. Descend the body angle by leaning, not by bending arms. Pure straight-arm scapular + anterior shoulder strength — direct planche prep. Hold 3-10s leans, 3-5 sets.

wall_hspu.name: Wall HSPU
wall_hspu.cue: Hands shoulder-width, head to floor, press to full lockout. Ribs closed.

x90_degree_hspu_negative.name: 90-Degree HSPU Negative
x90_degree_hspu_negative.cue: Slowly lower from a handstand while "seesawing" the body horizontal until you catch a bent-arm planche position (head + chest at 90°). The fusion of HSPU eccentric with planche bottom position. Multi-year skill.

freestanding_hs.name: Freestanding HS
freestanding_hs.cue: Balance with finger pressure. Micro-wrist adjustments. Breathe and relax.

handstand_push_up.name: Handstand Push-Up
handstand_push_up.cue: Freestanding handstand push-up. From a balanced freestanding handstand, lower head to floor under control, press back to full lockout. No wall, no kick assist. The HSPU benchmark for elite calisthenics. Build to 5 strict.

handstand_to_planche_negative.name: Handstand to Planche Negative
handstand_to_planche_negative.cue: Start in a solid handstand. Arms locked. Slowly lower the body down through straddle or full layout, attempting to catch and freeze the movement right at the horizontal planche line. The eccentric forces the CNS to adapt to full planche load.

straddle_planche.name: Straddle Planche
straddle_planche.cue: Legs straddled. Maintain hollow body. Years of work to reach here.

full_90_degree_hspu.name: Full 90-Degree HSPU
full_90_degree_hspu.cue: Lower from handstand into a bent-arm horizontal hold (the 90° planche position) and press back up to vertical handstand. Combines full HSPU range with planche-tier shoulder strength. The pinnacle of vertical+horizontal push fusion. Endpoint.

full_planche.name: Full Planche
full_planche.cue: Full straight-body planche hold. Legs together, body parallel to floor, shoulders over (and past) wrists. The pinnacle of straight-arm pushing strength. 3-5 second hold = elite. Multi-year skill — wrist conditioning mandatory.

planche_push_up.name: Planche Push-Up
planche_push_up.cue: From a full planche hold, lower body to chest-to-floor maintaining the planche position (no leg drop), press back to the planche. Hardest bodyweight push movement that exists in calisthenics. 1-3 strict reps = elite.

press_to_handstand.name: Press to Handstand
press_to_handstand.cue: From standing pike (forward fold), press straight into freestanding handstand without jumping or kicking. Pure compression + straight-arm pressing strength. Combines straddle/pike flexibility with planche-tier shoulder strength. Multi-year goal.

coaching.why: Two minutes of this is why your shoulder stops aching at a desk.
cues: Arms straight, band at chest height.
Pull apart until the hands are wide, squeeze the shoulder blades.
Return slowly — the way back is the half that counts.
mistakes: Shrugging. Shoulders down and away from the ears.

dead_hang.name: Dead Hang
dead_hang.cue: Passive full hang. Decompress the spine, build grip.

coaching.why: Grip, shoulders and a spine that gets to decompress, for the price of hanging on.
cues: Full grip, arms straight, shoulders relaxed but not collapsed.
Breathe. Let the spine lengthen.
Build the time before you build anything else.
mistakes: Dropping off the bar. Step down under control.

benchmark.standard: passive hang; full extension; no kipping

incline_row.name: Incline Row
incline_row.cue: High bar, body fairly upright. Row chest to bar.

scap_pushup.name: Scapular Push-Up
scap_pushup.cue: Arms locked straight. Push the floor away so the shoulder blades spread, then let the chest sink between them. The elbows never bend.

coaching.why: The first inch of a pull-up, and the piece almost everyone skips.
cues: Hang straight, then pull the shoulder blades down without bending the arms.
Tiny movement. Big difference.

australian_pullup.name: Australian Pull-Up
australian_pullup.cue: Bar at hip height, straight body, chest to bar. Feet forward = harder.

band_assisted_pullup.name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
band_assisted_pullup.cue: Band under feet/knee removes weight. Step down band thickness to progress.

coaching.why: The bridge between hanging and a real pull-up. Needs both the bar and a band.
cues: Loop the band over the bar and put one foot in it.
Thinner band each time you get comfortable.

jumping_pullup.name: Jumping Pull-Up
jumping_pullup.cue: Assist the concentric with a small jump, control the descent.

negative_pullup.name: Negative Pull-Up
negative_pullup.cue: Jump to the top, lower 3-5s. Builds the pull eccentrically.

straight_arm_lat_raise.name: Straight-Arm Lat Raise
straight_arm_lat_raise.cue: Straight arms, drive the bar down / hips up with the lats only. The front-lever base.

band_front_lever.name: Band-Assisted Front Lever
band_front_lever.cue: Band under the hips supports the lever. Thinner band to progress.

neutral_pullup.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
neutral_pullup.cue: Palms facing — kindest on the elbows and forearm.

seal_row.name: Seal Row
seal_row.cue: Prone on a bench, row the dumbbells — no momentum, pure back.

wide_inverted_row.name: Wide Inverted Row
wide_inverted_row.cue: Wide grip inverted row — upper back and lats.

coaching.why: The step between rowing a bell and pulling your own bodyweight.
cues: Body straight from ear to heel, chest to the bar.
Squeeze the shoulder blades before the arms bend.
The higher the bar, the easier — start high.
mistakes: Hips leading. The whole plank moves as one.

bent_over_row.name: Bent-Over Row
bent_over_row.cue: Hinge over, flat back, row to the ribs. DB or barbell.

coaching.why: Both sides at once, once one bell stops being enough load.
cues: Hinge, flat back, bells hanging straight down.
Lead with the elbows, pull to the hips.

feet_elevated_ring_row.name: Feet-Elevated Ring Row
feet_elevated_ring_row.cue: Feet up on a box — nearly horizontal, much harder.

pullup.name: Pull-Up
pullup.cue: Dead-hang start, chin over bar, controlled descent.

coaching.why: The one everybody wants. It is a long road and it starts with hanging.
cues: Dead hang, shoulders pulled down first.
Chin over the bar, chest towards it.
Lower slowly — the way down builds the way up.
mistakes: Kipping to get up. Not yet.

single_arm_row.name: Single-Arm Row
single_arm_row.cue: Square hips, drive elbow back, full stretch.

tuck_fl_raise.name: Tuck Front Lever Raise
tuck_fl_raise.cue: From dead hang, pull dynamically up into a tuck front lever, lower under control.

adv_tuck_front_lever.name: Advanced-Tuck Front Lever
adv_tuck_front_lever.cue: Open the tuck — hips extended, flat back, knees still bent.

archer_row.name: Archer Row
archer_row.cue: One arm pulls, the other stays straight out to the side.

commando_pullup.name: Commando Pull-Up
commando_pullup.cue: Straddle the bar, pull side to side, alternate lead hand.

explosive_pullup.name: Explosive Pull-Up
explosive_pullup.cue: Pull as high and fast as possible — power for the muscle-up.

german_hang.name: German Hang
german_hang.cue: Inverted hang, shoulders fully extended behind. Mobility + strength.

high_pullup.name: High Pull-Up
high_pullup.cue: Pull to lower-chest / waist height — the height a muscle-up needs.

pull_over.name: Pull-Over
pull_over.cue: Pull, then roll the hips over the bar to support. Transition builder.

single_arm_ring_row.name: Single-Arm Ring Row
single_arm_ring_row.cue: One arm, feet forward. Fight the rotation.

towel_pullup.name: Towel Pull-Up
towel_pullup.cue: Pull-ups gripping two towels — brutal grip and forearm.

band_muscle_up.name: Band-Assisted Muscle-Up
band_muscle_up.cue: Band assists the transition. Grease the whole movement.

chest_to_bar.name: Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up
chest_to_bar.cue: Pull higher — sternum to the bar. Muscle-up prep.

l_sit_pullup.name: L-Sit Pull-up
l_sit_pullup.cue: Hold the L, full pull — back + core.

negative_muscle_up_bar.name: Negative Muscle-Up (Bar)
negative_muscle_up_bar.cue: Start on top of the bar, lower slowly through the transition.

one_arm_hang.name: One-Arm Hang
one_arm_hang.cue: Hang from one arm 5-10s. Builds toward one-arm pulling.

single_leg_fl_raise.name: Single-Leg FL Raise
single_leg_fl_raise.cue: Raise with one leg extended straight.

single_leg_front_lever.name: Single-Leg Front Lever
single_leg_front_lever.cue: One leg straight, one tucked. Switch sides.

skin_cat_front_support.name: Skin the Cat to Front Support
skin_cat_front_support.cue: Pull through the German hang back up to a front support.

archer_pullup.name: Archer Pull-Up
archer_pullup.cue: One arm bends, the other stays straight. Shift side to side.

around_world_pullup.name: Around-the-World Pull-Up
around_world_pullup.cue: Arc side to side over the bar in a U shape.

false_grip_pullup.name: False-Grip Pull-Up
false_grip_pullup.cue: Wrists over the rings (false grip). The ring muscle-up gateway.

front_lever_row.name: Front Lever Row
front_lever_row.cue: From a front-lever line, row the body up to the bar. Elite back.

ice_cream_maker.name: Ice Cream Maker
ice_cream_maker.cue: From a front lever, pull to an inverted/pull-up top. Front-lever-to-bar.

straddle_fl_raise.name: Straddle FL Raise
straddle_fl_raise.cue: Raise into a straddle front lever.

straddle_front_lever.name: Straddle Front Lever
straddle_front_lever.cue: Legs straight and wide — shortens the lever vs full.

typewriter_pullup.name: Typewriter Pull-Up
typewriter_pullup.cue: At the top, slide side to side keeping the chin above the bar.

front_lever_pullup.name: Front Lever Pull-Up
front_lever_pullup.cue: Pull-up while holding the front-lever line. Extreme.

full_fl_raise.name: Full FL Raise
full_fl_raise.cue: Raise into a full front lever — elite.

full_front_lever.name: Full Front Lever
full_front_lever.cue: Body dead straight and horizontal. The goal hold.

muscle_up_bar.name: Muscle-Up (Bar)
muscle_up_bar.cue: Explosive pull, transition elbows over the bar, press out.

muscle_up_rings.name: Muscle-Up (Rings)
muscle_up_rings.cue: False grip, deep transition, press to support on rings.

one_arm_negative.name: One-Arm Negative Pull-Up
one_arm_negative.cue: One arm, slow lower only. Assist gently with the free hand.

one_arm_pullup.name: One-Arm Pull-Up
one_arm_pullup.cue: The elite pull — full range, one arm.

crunch.name: Crunch
crunch.cue: Lie on back, knees bent. Curl the shoulder blades off the floor by flexing the abs — don't yank the neck. Lower with control. Top-ab spinal flexion.

incline_plank.name: Incline Plank
incline_plank.cue: Hands on bench, body straight head to heel. Reduce bench height to progress.

lying_knee_tuck.name: Lying Knee Tuck
lying_knee_tuck.cue: Lie on back, hands by hips or under the glutes. Draw the knees toward the chest, curling the hips slightly off the floor. Lower-ab entry movement.

bear_hold.name: Bear Hold
bear_hold.cue: Bear-crawl position held still: hands under shoulders, knees hovering an inch off the floor, back flat. Squeeze everything and hold. A held bear crawl — brutal deep-core tension.

bent_knee_hollow_hold.name: Bent-Knee Hollow Hold
bent_knee_hollow_hold.cue: Lift the shoulder blades off the floor, knees bent at 90°, arms extended straight back behind the ears. Low back pressed flat. The easier hollow — keeps the legs light to protect the lower back.

bird_dog.name: Bird Dog
bird_dog.cue: On all fours. Extend the right arm forward and the left leg straight back at the same time. Hold 2 sec without letting the hips rotate, then switch sides. Anti-rotation control.

dead_bug.name: Dead Bug
dead_bug.cue: Lie on back, arms up, knees bent to 90°. Press the low back into the floor. Lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor slowly, then return to center. Brace the whole time.

coaching.why: Teaches the brace you will need the second a kettlebell leaves the floor.
cues: On your back, arms straight up, knees over hips at 90°.
Press the lower back flat into the mat and keep it there.
Lower one arm and the opposite leg. Only as far as the back stays flat.
mistakes: The lower back lifting off the mat. That is the exercise ending, whatever your limbs are doing.

flutter_kicks.name: Flutter Kicks
flutter_kicks.cue: Legs straight, heels six inches off the floor, low back pressed down. Alternate small fast up-down kicks. Keep the core braced the whole set.

foot_supported_l_sit.name: Foot-Supported L-Sit
foot_supported_l_sit.cue: Beginner L-sit: hands pressing down on the floor (or parallettes), knees bent or heels lightly touching the floor. Press the shoulders down and lift the chest. Build the compression before going feet-up.

reverse_crunch.name: Reverse Crunch
reverse_crunch.cue: Knees at 90°. Curl the pelvis up toward the ribs — lift the hips off the floor using the lower abs, not a leg swing. Slow eccentric.

scissor_kicks.name: Scissor Kicks
scissor_kicks.cue: Legs straight, heels off the floor. Cross one leg over the other in a scissor motion, alternating. Low back stays glued to the floor.

sit_up.name: Sit-Up
sit_up.cue: Full range — shoulder blades up to the knees and back down. Knees bent, feet planted. Drive through the abs, not momentum. Classic top-ab builder.

superman.name: Superman
superman.cue: Prone on floor. Simultaneously raise arms, chest, and legs off the ground. Hold 2 sec. Lower with control. Great lower back and posterior chain activation.

toe_touch_crunch.name: Toe Touch Crunch
toe_touch_crunch.cue: Legs straight up toward the ceiling. Reach the hands toward the toes, curling the upper back off the floor. Squeeze the upper abs at the top.

alternating_single_leg_l_sit.name: Alternating Single-Leg L-Sit
alternating_single_leg_l_sit.cue: Glutes lifted, arms locked. Lift one foot off the floor, hold a few seconds, tap it down, then lift the other — march the legs (bent-knee or straight-leg style). Builds toward zero foot support.

bear_hold_taps.name: Bear Hold Taps
bear_hold_taps.cue: From a static bear hold (knees hovering an inch off the floor), slowly tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, then switch. Keep the hips dead-even — no rotation. Anti-rotation under load.

bicycle_crunch.name: Bicycle Crunch
bicycle_crunch.cue: Lying crunch: opposite elbow to opposite knee in a pedaling motion. Slow and controlled beats fast and sloppy. Obliques + hip flexors.

bodyline_drill.name: Bodyline Drill
bodyline_drill.cue: Face down on floor. Arms straight overhead. Squeeze everything: glutes, core, quads, push armpits toward ears. Body is one rigid plank. The fundamental shape that all handstand work requires.

forearm_plank.name: Forearm Plank
forearm_plank.cue: Elbows under shoulders. Neutral spine. Posterior pelvic tilt. Squeeze glutes. No sagging or piking.

coaching.why: The brace that protects your back in every other movement here.
cues: Elbows under shoulders, forearms flat.
Squeeze the glutes, tuck the ribs down, pull the belly in.
Twenty honest seconds beats sixty sagging ones.
mistakes: Hips high in a tent. Flat line from shoulder to heel or it does not count.

hanging_knee_raise.name: Hanging Knee Raise
hanging_knee_raise.cue: From dead hang, pull knees to chest. Control the descent. No swinging.

coaching.why: Core work that also builds the grip and the hang at the same time.
cues: Hang still, then lift the knees to hip height.
No swinging. Stop the body before the next rep.

high_plank.name: High Plank
high_plank.cue: Arms straight, wrists under shoulders. Body rigid head to heel. Active shoulders — push the floor away.

hollow_body_crunch.name: Hollow Body Crunch
hollow_body_crunch.cue: From a full hollow hold, crunch the ribs toward the pelvis a few inches and return without losing the hollow line. Constant tension on the deep core — a hollow-position crunch.

hollow_hold.name: Hollow Hold
hollow_hold.cue: Lower back pressed flat. Ribcage closed. Arms overhead. Foundation of all gymnastics.

coaching.why: The shape every hard movement later is built on.
cues: Lower back pressed flat into the mat. That is the whole exercise.
Bend the knees and keep the arms by your side to start.
Only straighten out once the back stays flat.
mistakes: A gap under the lower back. Bend the knees more and keep the gap closed.

lying_leg_raise.name: Lying Leg Raise
lying_leg_raise.cue: Lie flat, legs straight. Raise the legs to vertical keeping them straight, then lower slowly without letting the heels touch. Hands under the glutes to protect the low back.

russian_twist.name: Russian Twist
russian_twist.cue: Sit at 45° lean, feet off floor. Rotate torso side to side. Touch ground each side. Add weight to progress.

side_plank.name: Side Plank
side_plank.cue: Knees bent 90°. Hip stacked, not sagging. Free hand on hip or extended up. 30-60 sec per side.

coaching.why: The side of the middle that the plank misses — and the bit that holds you upright in a carry.
cues: On one forearm, elbow under the shoulder, knees bent to start.
Lift the hips until you are one straight line.
Build to straight legs over weeks, not in one session.
mistakes: Hips drifting backwards. Stack shoulder, hip and knee.

tuck_up.name: Tuck-Up
tuck_up.cue: Lie flat, arms overhead, legs hovering. Crunch up while pulling both knees deeply into the chest, reach the hands past the feet at the peak balancing on the glutes, then open back to flat. The bent-knee V-up.

bear_limb_lift.name: Bear Limb Lift
bear_limb_lift.cue: Hold the hovering bear position and lift just one hand OR one foot slightly off the ground, hold briefly, return, then alternate. Two-point stability — fight the urge to shift your weight.

bear_opposing_limb_lift.name: Bear Opposing Limb Lift
bear_opposing_limb_lift.cue: From the bear hold, lift the opposing arm and leg (right arm + left leg) at once, hold 2-3 sec, then switch. The hardest bear variation — maximal anti-rotation and balance.

dragon_flag_candlestick.name: Dragon Flag Candlestick
dragon_flag_candlestick.cue: Grip a sturdy anchor behind the head. Roll the hips back, kick straight legs vertical (weight on the upper back, not neck), then lower the hips down rolling the spine one vertebra at a time. The hip-lift base.

pike_compression.name: Pike Compression Lifts
pike_compression.cue: Seated on floor, legs straight. Actively flex hip flexors to fold chest toward legs. Each rep is a muscular contraction — not gravity. THE L-sit/V-sit builder.

plank_leg_lift.name: Plank Leg Lift
plank_leg_lift.cue: Forearm plank. Lift one leg 6 inches — squeeze glute at top. No hip rotation. Hold 2 sec. Alternate.

plank_opposite_arm_leg.name: Plank Opposite Arm + Leg
plank_opposite_arm_leg.cue: High plank: extend opposite arm and leg simultaneously. Hold 2 sec at top. Anti-rotation + anti-extension in one movement. Bird-dog in plank position.

shoulder_tap.name: Plank Shoulder Taps
shoulder_tap.cue: High plank. Tap opposite shoulder — fight the rotation. Wider foot stance for more stability.

single_leg_v_up.name: Single-Leg V-Up
single_leg_v_up.cue: Sit up dynamically throwing ONE straight leg up, reaching both hands to touch that foot at the peak. Lower with control, alternate sides. Half the lower-body load of a full V-up.

straddle_v_up.name: Straddle V-Up
straddle_v_up.cue: Sit up opening both straight legs wide into a V straddle, reaching the hands through the center to the floor or ankles. Wide legs shorten the lever — easier than a closed-leg V-up.

tuck_l_sit.name: Tuck L-Sit
tuck_l_sit.cue: Knees tucked to chest in L-sit position. Build to 10s before extending legs.

tuck_v_sit_hold.name: Tuck V-Sit Hold
tuck_v_sit_hold.cue: From parallel bars or floor. Arms locked, scapula depressed. Tuck knees to chest, feet OFF floor. Build to 3x15s before extending legs.

v_up.name: V-Up
v_up.cue: Lie flat, arms overhead. Simultaneously lift legs and torso to meet in a V, hands toward feet. Lower under control — no slamming down.

bird_dog_crunch.name: Bird Dog Crunch
bird_dog_crunch.cue: Extend, then draw elbow-to-knee under body.

dragon_flag.name: Dragon Flag (Tuck)
dragon_flag.cue: From the vertical candlestick, knees tucked, lock the hips so torso and thighs are one rigid line and lower slowly (5-sec negative) until the lower back touches. Slow negatives (reps) OR hold parallel.

elevated_feet_plank.name: Elevated Feet Plank
elevated_feet_plank.cue: High plank with feet on bench. More load shifts to upper core and shoulders. 30-60 sec.

hanging_leg_raise.name: Hanging Leg Raise
hanging_leg_raise.cue: No swing. Posterior pelvic tilt at top. Control the descent. Legs straight.

hollow_rocks.name: Hollow Rocks
hollow_rocks.cue: From hollow body hold, rock forward and back like a rocking chair. No momentum — all core.

long_lever_plank.name: Long-Lever Plank
long_lever_plank.cue: Forearm plank but hands extended further forward. Increases the lever arm dramatically. Pure anti-extension strength.

plank_updown.name: Plank Up-Downs
plank_updown.cue: Start in forearm plank. Press up one hand at a time to high plank, then lower back down one hand at a time. Alternate the leading arm. Fight rotation throughout.

rkc_plank.name: RKC Plank
rkc_plank.cue: Posterior pelvic tilt, squeeze fists and glutes hard. 10s sets are enough.

side_plank_hip_dip.name: Side Plank Hip Dip
side_plank_hip_dip.cue: Full side plank: lower hip toward floor without touching, drive back up. Oblique-focused. 10-15 reps each side.

side_plank_leg_raise.name: Side Plank Leg Raise
side_plank_leg_raise.cue: Full side plank: raise top leg to hip height and lower with control. Abductors and obliques working simultaneously.

walk_up_plank.name: Walk-Up Planks
walk_up_plank.cue: Walk hands out to plank and back; long body.

ab_wheel_rollout.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
ab_wheel_rollout.cue: Hips must not sag at extension. Pull from abs — not hip flexors — to return.

copenhagen_plank.name: Copenhagen Plank
copenhagen_plank.cue: Top leg on bench, bottom leg floating. Straight body. Insane adductor + core.

hollow_to_v_sit_snap_up.name: Hollow-to-V-Sit Snap-Up
hollow_to_v_sit_snap_up.cue: From a low full hollow hold (heels 6 inches up), snap up into a full V-up touching the toes, then drop back into a rock-solid frozen hollow — no floor rest. Elite eccentric core control.

l_sit.name: L-Sit Hold
l_sit.cue: Arm lockout, depress scapulae, legs parallel to floor. Build tuck first.

one_leg_l_sit.name: One-Leg L-Sit
one_leg_l_sit.cue: From a tuck L-sit (glutes off floor), keep one knee tucked and extend the other leg dead straight out parallel to the floor, toes pointed. Switch legs. Hold, or do dynamic kick-outs. Bridges tuck → full L-sit.

plank_bodysaw.name: Plank Bodysaw
plank_bodysaw.cue: Forearm plank on sliders or socks. Slide body forward and pull back. Anti-extension at its hardest. Keep hips from sagging.

squeeze_loaded_hollow_hold.name: Squeeze-Loaded Hollow Hold
squeeze_loaded_hollow_hold.cue: Full hollow hold with a yoga block or ball squeezed between the ankles and a light plate held overhead. Squeeze hard — irradiation multiplies the load on the lower abs. Elite hollow.

straddle_l_sit.name: Straddle L-Sit
straddle_l_sit.cue: Legs spread wide in straddle rather than parallel. Easier to hold than strict L-sit. Good stepping stone to V-sit.

toes_to_bar.name: Toes-to-Bar
toes_to_bar.cue: Posterior pelvic tilt. Touch toes to bar. Minimize kip. Control descent.

tuck_dragon_flag_hold.name: Tuck Dragon Flag Hold
tuck_dragon_flag_hold.cue: Tucked, lower the rigid body until the torso hovers 2-3 inches parallel above the bench and freeze — weight on the shoulder blades and arms. Static tuck dragon flag.

hanging_inverted_hold.name: Hanging Inverted Hold
hanging_inverted_hold.cue: Pull the toes to the bar then keep tilting the hips back until the feet point at the ceiling — body upside down, tucked or straight. Depress the scapula hard. Balance shifts to the upper back and deep core.

jamaican_plank.name: Jamaican Plank
jamaican_plank.cue: From high plank, rotate into star side plank (top arm + top leg raised), hold 1 sec, rotate back through center plank, then rotate to the other side. Non-stop alternating. Also called alternating star plank or rotating star plank.

one_leg_v_sit.name: One-Leg V-Sit
one_leg_v_sit.cue: From the high tuck V-sit (leaning back, knees high), keep one knee tucked to the shoulder and kick the other leg straight up high toward the ceiling, above head height. Alternate legs.

ring_l_sit.name: Ring L-Sit
ring_l_sit.cue: L-sit on rings. Fight rotation — rings want to turn inward. Much harder than parallettes due to instability. Builds serious core and lat strength.

single_arm_plank.name: Single Arm Plank
single_arm_plank.cue: High plank — remove one arm. Fight hard to prevent rotation. Start at 10-15 sec per side. Build from there.

single_leg_dragon_flag.name: Single-Leg Dragon Flag
single_leg_dragon_flag.cue: One leg straight (locked knee, pointed toe), the other knee tucked. Keeping a dead-rigid waistline, lower until parallel to the bench. Switch legs. Slow negatives (reps) OR hold. Bridges tuck → full.

star_side_plank.name: Star Side Plank
star_side_plank.cue: Side plank: raise top arm and top leg simultaneously into full star shape. Maximum stability demand on every plane.

straddle_v_sit.name: Straddle V-Sit
straddle_v_sit.cue: Lean the torso back, push the hips up, launch both straight legs wide into a high V straddle, knees locked. Wide legs shorten the lever — the gateway to the full V-sit.

windshield_wipers.name: Windshield Wipers
windshield_wipers.cue: Hang from bar. Legs together, rotate side to side. Oblique gold.

single_arm_leg_plank.name: Single Arm + Leg Plank
single_arm_leg_plank.cue: One arm, opposite leg lifted. Two-point plank. Hardest plank variation. Master single arm before attempting.

v_sit.name: V-Sit
v_sit.cue: Legs above horizontal. Lean torso slightly back to counterbalance. Active compression.

inverted_candle.name: Inverted Candle
inverted_candle.cue: From the inverted hang, lock a straight line shoulders-to-toes (a vertical candle), then slowly lower the straight body toward horizontal, pivoting only at the shoulders. The ultimate suspension test (hanging dragon flag).

handstand.name: Freestanding Attempts
handstand.cue: Kick to balance, ride it as long as you can, bail safely.

front_lever_tuck.name: Front Lever Tuck
front_lever_tuck.cue: Gentle while forearm heals. Posterior tilt.

kick_up_practice.name: Kick-Up Practice
kick_up_practice.cue: Freestanding entries — find the balance point, bail to a cartwheel.

wall_handstand_hold.name: Wall Handstand Hold
wall_handstand_hold.cue: Chest to wall version: hands ~6in from wall. Hollow body, active shoulders. Chest-to-wall is harder than back-to-wall — less arch, more true handstand position.

mountain_climber.name: Mountain Climbers
mountain_climber.cue: From a high plank, drive the knees to the chest one at a time, fast. Hips stay low, shoulders stacked over hands, core braced. Multi-purpose: plank-hold core + shoulder/push stability + conditioning — used across core, push, and conditioning work.

coaching.why: Your heart rate, without a single jump on that ankle.
cues: Plank position, hands under shoulders.
Drive one knee to the chest, swap. Hips stay level.
Pace it. This is a thirty-second effort, not a sprint.
mistakes: Hips bouncing up and down. Slow it until they stop.

benchmark.standard: hips level; continuous knee drive; no piking

burpee.name: Burpee
burpee.cue: Squat-jump back-push-up-jump forward-jump + clap overhead. Rhythm is everything.

coaching.why: Thirty seconds that decides whether your back joins in for the rest of the session.
cues: On hands and knees. Wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.
Breathe out and round the spine up. Breathe in and let it sag.
Move one vertebra at a time. Slower is the whole point.
mistakes: Rushing it like a warm-up you have to get through. It is the session, not the queue for it.

deep_squat_rock.name: Deep Squat Rocks
deep_squat_rock.cue: Sit deep, rock side to side.

coaching.why: Opens the ankle and the hip before anything asks them to work.
cues: Heels down. Put them on a book if they lift — that is the ankle, not a failure.
Hold the deepest squat you own and rock gently side to side.
Chest tall. You are opening the hip, not folding over it.
mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom. Slow rocking beats bounce every time, and your knee will agree.

hip_flexor_stretch.name: Hip-Flexor Stretch
hip_flexor_stretch.cue: Tall hips, posterior tilt, per side.

kb_deadlift.name: Kettlebell Deadlift
kb_deadlift.cue: Bell on the floor between the feet. Push the hips back until your hands reach it, back flat, shins near vertical. Stand by driving the floor away.

coaching.why: The first movement of the whole program. Everything a kettlebell does later is this, faster.
cues: Bell on the floor between your feet, feet about hip width.
Push the hips back until your hands reach it. Back stays flat, shins near vertical.
Stand up by driving the floor away and squeezing the glutes at the top.
mistakes: Squatting down to it. Hips back, not hips down — the knees only bend as much as the hips demand.

kb_rdl.name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
kb_rdl.cue: Start standing. Push the hips back and slide the bell down the thighs, knees soft and staying soft. Go until the hamstrings stop you.

coaching.why: The hamstring half of the hinge, and the reason your lower back stops taking the load.
cues: Start standing, bell in both hands in front of your thighs.
Push the hips back and slide the bell down your legs. Soft knees, they do not bend further.
Go until you feel the hamstrings, then stand tall.
mistakes: Rounding the back to get lower. The hamstrings decide the depth, not your ambition.

kb_floor_press.name: Kettlebell Floor Press
kb_floor_press.cue: On your back, knees bent, bell in one hand at the chest. Press to over the shoulder, not over the face. The floor stops the elbow — touch, pause, press.

coaching.why: Pressing with a hard stop at the bottom, so the sore shoulder never goes anywhere it does not want to.
cues: On your back on the mat, knees bent, bell in one hand at your chest.
Press straight up. The bell finishes over the shoulder, not the face.
Lower until the upper arm touches the mat, then go again.
mistakes: Bouncing the elbow off the floor. Touch, pause, press.

kb_press.name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
kb_press.cue: Bell racked on the forearm, wrist straight. Press up and slightly back until the arm is by the ear. Ribs down; the lower back does not help.

coaching.why: Overhead, once the shoulder and the arm have earned it.
cues: Bell in the rack position, resting on the forearm, wrist straight.
Press up and slightly back until the arm is by your ear.
Ribs down. The lower back does not help.
mistakes: Pressing through arm pain. This one waits for the GP tick and a quiet shoulder.

kb_high_pull.name: Kettlebell High Pull
kb_high_pull.cue: Swing as normal, then guide the elbow high and back as the bell floats. The hips still do all the work — the arm only steers.

coaching.why: A swing that finishes in a pull. Upper back work without anything to hang from.
cues: Swing as normal, then guide the elbow high and back as the bell floats.
The hips still do all the work.
mistakes: Pulling early with the arm. The bell must be weightless before the elbow moves.

kb_halo.name: Kettlebell Halo
kb_halo.cue: Hold the bell upside down by the horns at the chest. Circle it slowly around the head, close to the skull. Five each way, ribs down.

coaching.why: Shoulder prep with the bell in your hands — and the kindest thing you can do for a sore arm before pressing.
cues: Hold the bell upside down by the horns, close to your chest.
Circle it slowly around your head, close to the skull.
Five one way, five the other. Ribs stay down throughout.
mistakes: Leaning back as it goes behind you. Stand still and let the shoulders do the travelling.

goblet_march.name: Goblet March
goblet_march.cue: Bell at the chest, stand tall. Lift one knee to hip height, hold a beat, put it down. A plank you do standing up.

coaching.why: A plank you do standing up. Kind to the ankle, brutal on the middle.
cues: Bell at the chest, stand tall.
Lift one knee to hip height, hold a beat, put it down.
Ribs down, no leaning back.
mistakes: Rushing. One slow knee is worth five fast ones.

suitcase_carry.name: Suitcase Carry
suitcase_carry.cue: One bell, one hand, hanging by your side. Walk tall and resist the tilt — staying vertical is the exercise, not the walking.

coaching.why: Grip, core and posture at once, and it looks like nothing. Perfect for a small flat.
cues: One bell in one hand, hanging by your side. Stand tall.
Walk. Do not lean away from it — resist the tilt.
Swap hands and walk back.
mistakes: Leaning to the other side to balance. Staying vertical IS the exercise.

turkish_getup.name: Turkish Get-Up
turkish_getup.cue: Learn it in halves with no bell for the first two weeks. Every position is a stop; nothing flows until every stop is solid.

coaching.why: The best thing a kettlebell can teach a 45-year-old body. Five minutes of it is a whole session.
cues: Learn it in halves, with no bell at all, for the first two weeks.
Every position is a stop. Nothing flows until every stop is solid.
mistakes: Doing the whole thing on day one. It is six movements pretending to be one.

prying_goblet.name: Prying Goblet Squat
prying_goblet.cue: Hold the bell at the chest and sit into the deepest squat you have. Use the elbows to push the knees out, and rock. A stretch, not a set.

coaching.why: The bell in front is what lets you sit into a squat your knee is happy with.
cues: Hold the bell at your chest and sit into the deepest squat you have.
Use the elbows to gently push the knees out, and rock.
Let the weight pull you down. It is a stretch, not a set.
mistakes: Treating it as a squat rep. There is no standing up in a hurry here.

glute_bridge.name: Glute Bridge
glute_bridge.cue: Heels close to your bum, toes up. Drive through the heels and squeeze hard at the top for a full second. Ribs down — the glutes lift, not the lower back.

coaching.why: Wakes the glutes so your knee stops doing their job.
cues: On your back, heels close to your bum, toes up.
Drive through the heels and squeeze hard at the top for one full second.
Ribs down. The lift comes from the glutes, not the lower back.
mistakes: Arching the back at the top and calling it height. Less range, more squeeze.

box_squat.name: Bench Squat
box_squat.cue: Stand in front of a bench, feet a bit wider than the hips. Sit back until you touch it lightly, then stand. Touch — do not drop onto it.

coaching.why: A squat with a floor under it. The bench tells your knee exactly how far it is going.
cues: Stand in front of the bench, feet a bit wider than hips.
Sit back until you touch it lightly, then stand.
Touch. Do not drop onto it.
mistakes: Going deeper than the bench because it felt fine. Depth is earned in weeks, not in one set.

march_in_place.name: Fast March
march_in_place.cue: Knees high, arms driving, stay light. Both feet never leave the floor at once — this is the no-impact way to raise a heart rate.

coaching.why: Conditioning that a sore ankle and a downstairs neighbour can both live with.
cues: Knees high, arms driving, stay light.
Thirty seconds hard, thirty easy.
mistakes: Turning it into jogging. Both feet never leave the floor at once.

straight_bar_dip.name: Straight Bar Dip
straight_bar_dip.cue: Support over a straight bar, lean forward slightly, lower until the chest reaches the bar. Harder on the shoulder than parallel bars — earn it.

ring_dip_support_hold.name: Ring Dip Support Hold
ring_dip_support_hold.cue: Locked out on the rings, rings turned out, shoulders down. Stillness is the whole exercise.

arm_circles.name: Arm Circles
arm_circles.cue: One arm at a time. Ten big slow circles forward, ten backward. Wakes the shoulder up before you load it.

down_dog_up_dog.name: Down Dog to Up Dog
down_dog_up_dog.cue: Hips high in an upside-down V, then sweep the chest through and forward until the arms are straight. Hold five seconds at each end.

down_dog_up_dog_bar.name: Down Dog to Up Dog (hands on bar)
down_dog_up_dog_bar.cue: Same movement with your hands on a hip-height bar instead of the floor. Much easier on the wrists and shoulders.

deep_squat_thoracic.name: Deep Squat Hold + Chest Opening
deep_squat_thoracic.cue: Hold a rack upright or straps and sink into a squat as deep as feels fine — never into pain. Reach the free arm up and behind you and let your chest turn to follow your hand. Swap arms.

high_knee_march.name: Standing High-Knee March
high_knee_march.cue: March on the spot, driving each knee up to hip height. Stay tall. No jumping, no impact — knee-friendly swap for mountain climbers.

hip_90_90.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
hip_90_90.cue: Sit on the floor, both knees bent to about 90° — one shin in front of you, the other out to the side. Keep tall and rotate your hips to swap both legs to the other side. Slow and controlled. Opens the hips with zero stress on the knee.

coaching.why: Opens the hip so the hinge comes from the hip and not the lower back.
cues: Sit with one shin in front at 90°, the other out to the side at 90°.
Keep the chest tall and rotate both knees to the other side.
Go slowly. Stop where it gets sharp, not where it gets hard.
mistakes: Falling onto the hands to get across. Hands on the floor for balance is fine, throwing yourself over is not.

worlds_greatest_stretch.name: World's Greatest Stretch
worlds_greatest_stretch.cue: Step one foot forward into a gentle lunge, both hands on the floor inside the front foot. Reach the inside arm up to the ceiling and turn your chest to follow it. Bring it back down, step back, switch sides. Opens hips, chest and back in one move.

lat_pulldown.name: Lat Pulldown
lat_pulldown.cue: Sit tall, pull the bar to your upper chest and lead with your elbows, not your hands. Let it back up slowly.

seated_cable_row.name: Seated Cable Row
seated_cable_row.cue: Chest up, pull the handle to your belly and squeeze your shoulder blades together. Do not lean back to move the weight.

chest_supported_row.name: Chest-Supported Row
chest_supported_row.cue: Chest stays flat on the pad the whole set. Row to your ribs, pause a beat, lower slowly. The pad does the cheating for you.

face_pull.name: Face Pull
face_pull.cue: Rope at head height. Pull it toward your forehead and let your hands split apart at the end. Light weight, slow, feel it between the shoulder blades.

reverse_fly.name: Reverse Fly (chest-supported)
reverse_fly.cue: Chest flat on an incline bench, a light dumbbell in each hand hanging down. Arms almost straight, raise them out to the sides like opening your arms wide. Squeeze the back of your shoulders at the top, lower slowly. Light weight — this is never a heavy movement.

rear_delt_row.name: Chest-Supported Rear-Delt Row
rear_delt_row.cue: Chest on the incline bench, dumbbells hanging. Row them out WIDE with your elbows flared out to the sides, up toward your chest — not tucked to your ribs. The wide elbow path is what makes it hit the back of the shoulders. Squeeze, lower slow.

cable_rear_delt_fly.name: Cable Rear-Delt Fly
cable_rear_delt_fly.cue: Cable set at shoulder height. Grab the handle with the opposite hand so the cable crosses your body, arm almost straight. Pull it out and across, away from your body. Constant tension the whole way. One arm at a time.

prone_ytw.name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
prone_ytw.cue: Face down on an incline bench, arms hanging, thumbs up. Raise the arms into a Y overhead, lower. Then straight out to a T, lower. Then bent into a W, lower. That is one rep. No weight or very light — this is for the small muscles that hold your shoulders back.

barbell_curl.name: Barbell Curl
barbell_curl.cue: Elbows pinned to your sides. Curl up, lower all the way down under control. If your back is swinging, the bar is too heavy.

assisted_chinup_top_hold.name: Chin-Up Top Hold (assisted machine)
assisted_chinup_top_hold.cue: Palms facing you. Use the assist machine to get your chin above the bar, then just hold there. Chest up, shoulders down. Log the ASSIST weight: lower is stronger.

db_pullover.name: DB Pullover (on bench)
db_pullover.cue: Lie back on the bench holding one dumbbell over your chest, elbows slightly bent and fixed. Lower the dumbbell back to about head level only — feel the stretch across your lats and ribs, not deep in the shoulder. Pull it back over your chest. Start light, 20-25 lb.

db_shoulder_press.name: DB Shoulder Press
db_shoulder_press.cue: Sit tall, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height. Press straight overhead, ribs down so you do not arch your back. Lower back to ear height under control.

farmers_carry.name: Farmer's Carry (no straps)
farmers_carry.cue: A dumbbell in each hand, no straps — grip is the point. Walk tall, shoulders back, 30-40 m. Set them down when the round is done, not when your grip fails. If they slip early, go lighter. Start 40-50 lb per hand.

chest_press_machine.name: Chest Press Machine
chest_press_machine.cue: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the middle of your chest. Press out, control the way back. Do not lock out hard.

shoulder_press_machine.name: Shoulder Press Machine
shoulder_press_machine.cue: Press straight overhead, ribs down so you do not arch your back. Lower until your hands are about ear height.

assisted_dip.name: Assisted Dip (machine)
assisted_dip.cue: Kneel or stand on the pad — the machine takes weight off you. Lean forward a little, lower until your upper arms are level with the floor, press back up. Log the ASSIST weight: lower is stronger.

lateral_raise.name: Lateral Raise
lateral_raise.cue: Light dumbbells. Raise them out to the sides up to shoulder height, elbows soft. Lower slowly. This one is never heavy.

triceps_pushdown.name: Triceps Pushdown
triceps_pushdown.cue: Elbows glued to your sides. Push the bar or rope down until your arms are straight, then let it come back up slowly.

pushup_on_dumbbells.name: Push-Ups on Dumbbells
pushup_on_dumbbells.cue: Hands gripping two dumbbells set on the floor so your wrists stay straight. Body in one line, chest down between them, press back up.

db_rdl.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
db_rdl.cue: Push your hips back and slide the dumbbells down the front of your legs. Knees stay almost straight. Stop when you feel the stretch behind your thighs, then stand tall.

back_extension_45.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
back_extension_45.cue: Pad just below your hip bones. Bend at the hips and come back up until your body is one straight line — do not arch past that.

kb_swing.name: Kettlebell Swing
kb_swing.cue: Snap the hips — the arms are just rope. The bell floats up to chest height from your hips driving forward, not from lifting with your shoulders. Start at 12–16 kg.

coaching.why: The movement the whole thing has been building to. It arrives in week five, not week one.
cues: Hike the bell back between your legs like a rugby pass.
Snap the hips forward hard. The bell floats to chest height on its own.
Arms are rope. They do not lift anything.
mistakes: Squatting and lifting it with the shoulders. That is not a swing and it is how backs get hurt.

wall_sit.name: Wall Sit
wall_sit.cue: Back flat on the wall, slide down until your thighs are somewhere comfortable — the higher you stay, the easier on the knee. Hold still and breathe.

coaching.why: Quad strength with nothing moving — which is why the knee tolerates it when reps do not.
cues: Back flat on the wall, slide down until the thighs are where the knee is comfortable.
Hands off the thighs.
Breathe. Come out before the form goes.
mistakes: Going to ninety degrees because that is the picture. Go to where it does not hurt.

benchmark.standard: thighs parallel; back flat on the wall; hands off the thighs

spanish_squat.name: Spanish Squat
spanish_squat.cue: Thick band looped behind your knees and anchored in front of you. Sit back against the band and hold. Great for calming a cranky knee down.

banded_tke.name: Banded Terminal Knee Extension
banded_tke.cue: Band around the back of your knee, anchored in front. Straighten the knee against the band and squeeze the thigh. Tiny range, big effect — knee-friendly.

hip_abduction_machine.name: Hip Abduction Machine
hip_abduction_machine.cue: Pads on the outside of your knees. Push your knees apart, pause, come back slowly. Sit up tall.

hip_adduction_machine.name: Hip Adduction Machine
hip_adduction_machine.cue: Flip the pads to the inside of your knees. Squeeze your knees together, pause, let them open back out slowly.

hollow_heels_down.name: Hollow Hold (heels down)
hollow_heels_down.cue: Lie on your back with your heels resting on the floor. Lift only your shoulders off the ground and press your low back flat. Easiest version — nothing should pull on your back.

incline_side_plank.name: Side Plank (hand on bar)
incline_side_plank.cue: One hand on a hip-height bar, feet on the floor, body in a straight line. The higher the bar, the easier it is.
